A FEW WAYS IN

Follow your curiosity.

Drag or use arrows to orbit. Scroll / pinch / + − zooms. Mountain height raises the peaks; Valley depth lowers the depressions; Roughness adds fine ridges; Landscape depth stretches the range front to back. These changes preserve the seed. New terrain or R changes the seed while preserving the sliders and camera. Space switches Alpine, Contours, and Wireframe views. P pauses automatic orbit; every control and PNG capture still works while paused.

The mathematics

Five octaves of seeded, ridged value noise form a finite height field. Domain warping bends its ridges; roughness changes the contribution of finer noise. The sampled field is normalized once to [−1,1]. Mountain height H scales positive elevations and Valley depth V scales negative elevations independently, in relative units. Landscape depth stretches its front-to-back extent while preserving the same elevations. The 64 × 64 grid becomes 8,192 triangles. Shading and interpolated height contours reveal the relief; the dark sides show a cut section. This is a procedural landscape, without erosion or real-world elevation data.
